verdict.rationale: Gazebo's docs and GitHub description mention TCP/IP transport for running simulations on remote servers (gz-transport, socket-based messaging) and 'extensive command line tools for increased simulation introspection and control,' plus GUI plugins to 'introspect and interact with your simulations' — these give some remote-inspection capability. However, all evidence frames this around simulated worlds/servers, not a physically deployed robot in the field, and there's no mention of live log streaming or state/log aggregation tooling for a real robot. missing for 10: evidence of monitoring an actual deployed/physical robot (vs simulated server), log inspection tooling, and independent hands-on confirmation of remote debugging workflows.
